anchors.description: Full width of the wall-mounted whiteboard along its top edge, from the top-left frame corner to the top-right frame corner.
anchors.visible_evidence: Whiteboard frame edges traced continuously from corner (212,148) to (976,229); whole board spans ~768 px of the 1280-px image, board rectangle is planar and fully visible.
anchors.identity_uncertainty: Board model unknown; assumed standard ~1800x900 mm (2:1) whiteboard. 1200x900 or 2400x1200 boards would rescale this anchor by roughly 0.7-1.3x, offsetting all other anchors with it.

anchors.description: Height of the whiteboard along its left frame edge, from the top-left corner to the bottom-left corner.
anchors.visible_evidence: Left frame edge visible as a continuous near-vertical line from (212,148) to (221,653), ~505 px; board aspect after perspective correction is about 2:1.
anchors.identity_uncertainty: Same whiteboard prior as a1: standard 1800x900 mm assumed; a 4:3 board would change the implied height differently from the width estimate.

anchors.description: Length of the upper dry-erase marker resting in the whiteboard pen holder, from its red cap end to its far tip.
anchors.visible_evidence: Upper slot of the pen holder shows a red-capped marker with grey/green barrel; visible ends at about (943,501) and (982,500), ~39 px, consistent with a standard ~13-14 cm marker.
anchors.identity_uncertainty: Brand/format not readable; both ends partly shaded by the holder rails, so the visible extent may under-measure by 1-2 cm. Standard dry-erase markers range ~12-15 cm.

anchors.description: Long-axis length of the cream/pale-yellow whiteboard eraser attached near the lower right of the board, from its lower-left end to its upper-right end.
anchors.visible_evidence: Eraser block separated from the board by its higher saturation and brightness; min-area rectangle gives long axis from (916,444) to (943,408), ~46 px, short side ~20 px (ratio ~2.3 typical of a hand eraser).
anchors.identity_uncertainty: Generic whiteboard eraser; exact model unknown. Typical eraser blocks are 12-14 cm long, 5-6 cm wide; slight depth foreshortening and blur add ~10% uncertainty.
